quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
rationale: Section 6.1 is the only covenant in the Agreement that restrains our side (Section 6.3 restrains HDI, and for two years post-term, which favours us). It sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred "no restriction" position, and so is not redlined: (i) it runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under Section 4.1 is one year (auto-renewing, terminable on 90 days' notice), so the restraint never exceeds 12 months without our consent to renew; (ii) scope is limited by product and channel — Internet projects similar to the Site offering Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, with the competing products named (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — rather than the walk-away formulation of "any competing business"; and (iii) there is a carve-out in Section 6.2 for a closeout-merchandise site, and "Deerskin Products" itself excludes closeout goods and the Joan Cook Catalog. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (so acquiring a leather retailer that runs a competing site could implicate 6.1), and the words "companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled" are looser than a purely named-product limit. We would take these as clarifications if the document is reopened for other reasons, but they are not material enough to breach the fallback, and deletion of 6.1 would be disproportionate given HDI's heavier reciprocal restraint in Section 6.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no liability cap or damages exclusion, so we added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with a mutual consequential-damages waiver. Confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and the Company's payment obligations are not capped damages; we can discuss a straight twelve-months'-fees cap as a fallback.

ops.text: (c) Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000). Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages or lost profits. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments due under this Agreement (including any Termination Payment) shall not be treated as damages subject to this limitation.

proposal.summary: Insert mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1m), consequential-damages waiver and uncapped Excluded Claims into Section 9.

rationale: The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, no aggregate cap, and no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Searches for "liability", "damages", "consequential", "aggregate", "liable" and "indemnif" return nothing responsive — the only hits are the no-joint-venture language (p0061-p0062) and the Termination Payment calculation (p0026). The Warranties section (p0055-p0058) contains only representations plus a Globix carve-out, and General Provisions (p0059-p0070) has no liability terms. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited liability, including the Company for consequential losses arising from Content, marketing and payment matters, so the rule's fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs) is not met. We inserted the preferred mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential-damages waiver, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's payment obligations (including the Termination Payment) excluded from the cap. Placement as Section 9(c) also picks up the existing survival provision in Section 10.7, which covers Section 9.

The fallback level is a separate bargain and is not satisfied either: a greater-of cap exceeds the fallback "cap of 12 months' fees", so the insertion cannot be scored down to the fallback. quote: HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's
rationale: The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation obligation on the Company. A full read of the fee, exclusivity, cross-promotion and general provisions (§§ 3, 6, 7, 10) shows no requirement that the Company extend HDI its best terms, match third-party offers, or grant HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others. The only "no less favorably" undertaking (§ 1.8, p0013) runs in our favour: HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favourably than its own catalog titles. The § 7.1 cross-promotion covenant is a mutual "reciprocal and equitable basis" commitment rather than a favoured-terms obligation, and § 6.1 exclusivity is a separate commercial term addressed under the exclusivity rule. This meets the preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer, favoured treatment running to us), so no redline is proposed.

quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
rationale: The fee construct meets the preferred position: the Company's only payment obligation is a 30% share of actual Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold, i.e. purely usage/revenue-based with no guaranteed minimum, minimum hosting fee, committed volume or shortfall/take-or-pay mechanic anywhere in Section 3. The $11,000 figure operates as a floor below which no fee is payable (a benefit to us), not as a minimum commitment. Section 4.1 also gives a one-year term with annual renewal terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so there is no multi-year lock-in without an exit. Noted but not flagged here: the Section 4.2 Termination Payment (trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved) is an exit cost rather than a purchase commitment or shortfall penalty, and is better addressed under the termination-fee rule; the Section 6.1 exclusivity covenant is likewise a scope restriction rather than a volume cap, and is reviewed under the exclusivity rule. No redline required.

quote: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns binding clause: it imposes no consent requirement and no restriction on transfer by either party, and the Agreement contains no change-of-control language anywhere (searches for "change of control", "successor" and "consent" return nothing else relevant). Our side is therefore unconstrained (no blanket prohibition, no HDI termination or re-pricing right on our change of control), so this is not walk-away territory. But the fallback requires a consent standard for assignments other than to successors, and here HDI may freely assign this hosting and site-development engagement to any third party, including a competitor of ours, with no notice and no consent — a material failure of the fallback on the vendor side of a high-severity assignment rule. We propose the smallest edit reaching the preferred position: express affiliate/successor assignment freedom for the Company, a reasonableness-qualified consent gate plus competitor bar on HDI assignments, and confirmation that our change of control triggers no HDI right.

rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated termination payment payable by us (the Company) to HDI whenever we terminate — including on an ordinary 90-day non-renewal under Section 4.1 — measured as one half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000. Because our fees under Section 3.1 are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, this formula can exceed a full year's fees and is uncapped, so it fails the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees and approaches walk-away territory (penalty triggered by routine termination). Our preference is deletion; given HDI builds and hosts the Site at no upfront cost, we proposed the fallback three-month cap as the sole amount due on termination. The instalment mechanic in 4.2(c) is unobjectionable once capped, and the "without penalty" termination right in Section 1.6 runs in our favour.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience exit on 90 days' written notice against a one-year auto-renewing term, which sits at our fallback on notice period and on HDI's symmetrical (end-of-term) right — that element we do not redline. The material failure is Section 4.2: if the Company terminates, it owes an uncapped Termination Payment equal to 50% of Net Sales above $800,000 for the trailing twelve months, payable over eight quarterly installments. Because fees to HDI are only 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month, that formula can exceed a full year's fees and far exceeds the fallback ceiling of three months' fees, so the Company has no genuinely penalty-free exit. We therefore capped the Termination Payment at three months' fees (fallback rather than preferred, given HDI's site build investment and the revenue-share bargain).

verification.notes: All four atomic fallback elements are operative: a Customer convenience right at 90 days (within the 60–90 day band), a cap on the Termination Payment at 3 months' fees, and an HDI convenience right confined to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice. Preferred fails on three independent elements: notice is 90 rather than 30 days, there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and HDI retains a (limited) convenience right rather than none during a committed term. Consistent with the locked fallback target. Minimality holds: two surgical edits — one concise insertion supplying the absent convenience-termination mechanic, and a short proviso appended to the existing Termination Payment formula rather than a rewrite of 4.2(a). The bracketed gloss 'for this purpose "Customer" means the Company' is a necessary alias bridge because the agreement names the customer 'the Company', so it is not surplus. Intent preserved: the one-year term, automatic renewal, either-party 90-day non-renewal notice, the Net Sales-based Termination Payment formula and the eight-quarterly-instalment payment mechanic in 4.2(c) all remain effective; the new proviso only caps, and does not displace, the formula. Noted in rationale only (not a deviation): 'fees' is not a defined term in this Net Sales-based agreement, so the cap would read more cleanly tied to a defined revenue/fee metric; and the preferred pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts was not obtained.
